newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mkt shortage jumps to over 9 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African mkt shortage jumps to over 9 bln rand.

text.p: The money market shortage surged 850 million rand to over nine billion rand on Monday as a result of foreign exchange flows, dealers said.
Reserve Bank figures released on Tuesday show the shortage at 9.123 billion rand on Monday from 8.273 billion rand on Saturday.
Andre Kock, the central bank's head of money markets, said there was nothing dramatic about the spike in the shortage.
"The shortage reflects flows in the foreign exchange market," Kock said, "one shouldn't read too much into it,"
He added that the shortage was expected to ease again over the next couple of days.
Traders said the market had been unaffected by the rise in the shortage and that it was expected to return to its recent 8.0 to 8.5 billion rand range on Tuesday.
Three-month NCDs were static at between 16.10 and 15.90 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was steady at 15.50 to 15.35 percent.
